interest: This file provides valuable historical insight into the legal, diplomatic, and financial complications surrounding pre-war Japanese dollar debts during the Allied Occupation of Japan. It documents the conflict between the Securities and Exchange Commission's desire to end an informal, legally questionable trading ban on Japanese securities and SCAP's deconcentration program, which sought to dissolve the 1938 electric power combine without being impeded by the reinstatement of pre-war mortgage liens abrogated by Japanese wartime legislation (Law No. 60 of 1943). Furthermore, the inquiries from diverse individual claimants—including high-ranking military officers like Major General Edgar Erskine Hume, SCAP civilian employees, private citizens, and estate attorneys—demonstrate the real-world impact of wartime asset freezes and illuminate the administrative limbo experienced by bondholders prior to the 1951 San Francisco Peace Treaty and the 1952 debt resumption settlements. The inclusion of an incongruous biographic roster of young Japanese Foreign Ministry diplomats also provides a unique glimpse into post-war Japanese diplomatic rehabilitation and leadership development.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.51 Bondholders, covering August to December 1949) documents United States policy, inter-agency deliberations, and public inquiries regarding pre-World War II Japanese government, municipal, and corporate dollar bonds held by American investors. Following the wartime suspension of trading on American exchanges and the Japanese government's enactment of Law No. 60 of 1943—which unilaterally cancelled corporate mortgage indentures and converted domestic dollar bonds into yen obligations—the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the Department of State, the Department of the Army, and SCAP debated the conditions necessary to lift the ban on trading Japanese dollar securities in the United States. High-level discussions addressed the dilemma of reinstating abrogated mortgage liens without disrupting SCAP's antitrust and economic deconcentration program against Japanese electric power combines, while acknowledging that Japan lacked foreign exchange for debt service. Concurrently, the file contains inquiries from individual bondholders and estate attorneys (including Major General Edgar Erskine Hume, SCAP employee Mary Michelin, Dr. A. L. Lewin, and attorney Emelyn L. MacKenzie) seeking guidance on the redemption, value, and claim procedures for their holdings in Imperial Japanese Government loans, City of Tokyo external bonds, and utility issues (such as Tokyo Electric Light, Ujigawa Electric Power, and Oriental Development Company). In response, the State Department consistently noted that no general claims fund existed, foreign investment involved private risk, and recovery would depend on future external debt settlements negotiated through the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, Inc. The file also contains an unrelated biographic list detailing four Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs officials slated for overseas study.

subfiles.about: Acknowledgment of General Edgar Erskine Hume's letter regarding his 1924 Japanese Government external loan bond and transmittal of the matter to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.
subfiles.from: Gardner E. Palmer, Special Assistant, Division of Financial Affairs, Department of State
keywords: Imperial Japanese Government External Loan of 1924
subfiles.summary: Gardner E. Palmer acknowledges receipt of Major General Edgar Erskine Hume's letter of August 25, 1949 regarding a $1,000 Imperial Japanese Government External Loan bond of 1924. Palmer confirms that the information has been placed on record for appropriate future reference. He informs General Hume that a copy has been forwarded to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, Inc. in New York, a non-profit entity representing bondholders in negotiating foreign debt settlements.

subfiles.to: Major General Edgar Erskine Hume, General Headquarters, Far East Command

subfiles.about: Transmittal of Major General Edgar Erskine Hume's letter and the Department's reply to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.

subfiles.summary: The Department of State transmits to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, Inc. in New York a copy of an inquiry from Major General Edgar Erskine Hume dated August 25, 1949. A copy of the Department's reply to General Hume is also enclosed for the Council's records and information.

subfiles.about: Notification by General Hume of his ownership of an Imperial Japanese Government gold bond and its transfer as a gift to his grandson.
subfiles.from: Major General Edgar Erskine Hume, Medical Section, General Headquarters, Far East Command
keywords: Imperial Japanese Government External Loan of 1924
subfiles.summary: Major General Edgar Erskine Hume reports his ownership of a $1,000 6.5% Imperial Japanese Government External Loan bond of 1924 (due February 1954, Number M-95902, with coupons attached from August 1941 onwards). Hume states that he discussed the bond with SCAP's Civil Property Custodian in Tokyo and was advised that no immediate action could be taken. He requests that his ownership be recorded by the State Department and notes that he has presented the bond to his two-year-old grandson, Edgar Erskine Hume, III, in Frankfort, Kentucky.
subfiles.title: Letter from Major General Edgar Erskine Hume to Occupation Areas Division
subfiles.to: Occupation Areas Division, Department of State

subfiles.about: Inter-agency conference between State, Army, SEC, and SCAP officials concerning the resumption of trading in Japanese dollar bonds, Law No. 60 of 1943, and the economic deconcentration program.
subfiles.from: Gardner E. Palmer, Division of Financial Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Officials from the Department of State, Department of the Army, Securities and Exchange Commission, and SCAP meet to discuss lifting the wartime ban on trading Japanese dollar bonds in the United States. SEC Commissioner Donald C. Cook emphasizes mounting pressure from over-the-counter dealers to resume trading, pointing out that the informal ban lacks legal enforcement power. Dr. Edward Welch of SCAP reviews Japanese Law No. 60 of 1943, which converted dollar bonds of merged utilities into yen obligations and cancelled their mortgage liens, explaining that SCAP's plan to break up the 1938 electric power combine would be hindered if original liens were restored. State Department officials argue that the unilateral abrogation of American lien rights cannot be accepted without protest and insist on establishing valid debt totals, while Deputy Under Secretary of the Army Robert West agrees to study the issues in Tokyo based on an SEC memorandum.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Japanese Dollar Bonds

subfiles.about: Inquiry regarding how to file a claim against the Japanese government for recovery of municipal and corporate gold bearer bonds.
subfiles.from: Mrs. Mary Michelin, Civil Property Custodian, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: Mrs. Mary Michelin, writing from Tokyo where she works with SCAP's Civil Property Custodian, requests advice from the Department of State on filing claims against the Japanese government. She seeks to recover investments in four gold bearer bonds: one City of Tokyo External Loan bond of 1927, one Ujigawa Electric Power Company first mortgage bond, and two Tokyo Electric Light Company first mortgage bonds. She inquires into the proper claims procedure and whether such filings should be submitted directly to the State Department.
subfiles.title: Letter from Mrs. Mary Michelin to Department of State Regarding Bond Claims

subfiles.about: Biographical sketches and foreign study interests of four Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs officials.
subfiles.summary: This document contains concise biographical sketches of four Japanese Foreign Office officials proposed for study or observation abroad. It details the ages, university education, personality evaluations, and professional interests of Katsumi Ono (Director of Political Affairs Bureau), Harumi Takeuchi (Chief of Second Section, Research Bureau), Jun Tsuchiya (GHQ Liaison Officer), and Yasuhiko Nara (Press Section, Political Affairs Bureau). The officials express interests in studying United Nations General Assembly operations, research methodology, international organization, and public relations and UNESCO cultural exchanges.
subfiles.title: Biographic Sketches of Japanese Foreign Ministry Officials

subfiles.about: Advice to Mrs. Michelin on the status of Japanese public utility and municipal bonds, vested assets, and debt settlement prospects.
subfiles.from: Office of Financial and Development Policy, Department of State
keywords: Office of Financial and Development Policy
subfiles.summary: The State Department responds to Mrs. Mary Michelin's inquiry, explaining that while the City of Tokyo and corporate utility bonds she holds are guaranteed by the Japanese government, no general claims procedure exists for bondholders. The letter explains that claims filed with the Office of Alien Property against Japanese government assets vastly exceeded available funds, leaving any distribution negligible, and that Congress and the War Claims Commission have yet to decide how residual vested assets will be treated. The Department advises that bondholder recovery will ultimately depend on future Japanese external debt settlements and recommends registering her holdings with the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, Inc.
subfiles.title: Letter from Office of Financial and Development Policy to Mrs. Mary Michelin
subfiles.to: Mrs. Mary Michelin, Civil Property Custodian, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Transmittal of the Department's response to Mrs. Mary Michelin's bond inquiry to the Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to the Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan in Tokyo a copy of Mrs. Mary Michelin's inquiry of November 30, 1949, along with the Department's formal reply. The instruction authorizes the diplomatic mission to forward the Department's response to Mrs. Michelin at its discretion.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 288 to the Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Inquiry concerning the current status and settlement prospects of two Tokyo General Electric Company bonds.
subfiles.summary: Dr. A. L. Lewin writes to Secretary of State Dean Acheson inquiring about the status of two bonds of the Tokyo General Electric Company. He references previous correspondence sent to General Douglas MacArthur in August 1946, which was answered in January 1947 with the explanation that business transactions could not proceed until foreign exchange policies were established. Lewin asks for updated information on the current status of the bonds and what steps he should take.
subfiles.title: Letter from Dr. A. L. Lewin to Secretary of State Dean Acheson

subfiles.about: Explanation of the Japanese government guarantee on Tokyo General Electric bonds and referral to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.
subfiles.from: Gardner E. Palmer, Adviser, Office of Financial and Development Policy, Department of State
keywords: Japan Electric Generation and Transmission Company
subfiles.summary: Gardner E. Palmer responds to Dr. A. L. Lewin's inquiry regarding two Tokyo General Electric Company bonds, noting that while originally corporate debts, they were guaranteed by the Japanese Government on April 1, 1939 upon consolidation into the Japan Electric Generation and Transmission Company, Ltd. Palmer explains that the Department views holding foreign securities as a private transaction subject to inherent investor risks, but notes that the government assists bondholders where feasible. He advises Dr. Lewin to register his bonds with the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, Inc. to stay informed of debt settlement negotiations.
subfiles.title: Letter from Gardner E. Palmer to Dr. A. L. Lewin

subfiles.about: Communication on legal letterhead from attorney John Hindrum Strahan regarding Japanese bondholders.
subfiles.from: John Hindrum Strahan, Counsellor at Law
subfiles.summary: This document is a formal letterhead communication from attorney John Hindrum Strahan of Newark, New Jersey, addressed to the Department of State. Received on December 7, 1949, and routed to the Claims Unit and Gardner E. Palmer, it concerns Japanese dollar bondholders filed under decimal classification 894.51.
subfiles.title: Letter from John Hindrum Strahan to Department of State

subfiles.about: Inquiry regarding the valuation and claim eligibility of an Oriental Development Company bond held by the Estate of Rosebud Levenson.
subfiles.from: Emelyn L. MacKenzie, Counselor at Law
subfiles.summary: Attorney Emelyn L. MacKenzie writes to the War Claims Division of the State Department on behalf of the Estate of Rosebud Levenson, who died in the Bronx, New York, on July 24, 1949. She states that the estate holds a $1,000 6% Oriental Development Company, Ltd. bond due in 1953 (bond number 16506, with coupons from March 1942 attached). MacKenzie requests information on the bond's value at the date of death and asks whether a claim can be asserted against Japanese assets vested in the United States based on the Imperial Japanese Government's guarantee.
subfiles.title: Letter from Emelyn L. MacKenzie to Department of State Regarding Estate of Rosebud Levenson
subfiles.to: War Claims Division, Department of State
